issues.t: Rough running and misfires with check engine light
issues.sym: The engine shakes or stumbles, especially when accelerating with a load, and the check engine light comes on or flashes.
issues.why: A rough-running engine with misfires is the most-reported E-350 problem on RepairPal. On these gas engines it is usually a worn spark plug, a failing coil-on-plug ignition coil or its rubber boot.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find the cylinder. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Front end rattles and loose steering
issues.sym: Rattling or clunking from the front over bumps, play in the steering wheel, wandering on the highway, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: These are heavy vans and chassis, and front suspension and steering parts such as ball joints, tie rod ends and bushings wear under the weight. RepairPal lists front-end rattling and play in the front wheels among common E-350 complaints.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected and aligned. Worn steering parts get worse quickly on a heavy vehicle and can affect control.

issues.t: Spark plug blows out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud popping or ticking like a gunshot under the engine cover, then a rough-running engine, loss of power and a check engine light.
issues.why: The aluminum heads on Ford's 4.6L, 5.4L and 6.8L engines of this era had only a few threads holding each spark plug. Over time a plug can work loose and shoot out, often stripping the threads and sometimes damaging the ignition coil.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as it is safe; the open hole can damage wiring and the coil. A shop can usually repair the threads with an insert without pulling the head.

issues.t: Cracked plastic intake manifold leaks coolant
issues.sym: A sudden coolant leak at the front top of the engine, a sweet smell, steam, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Early 4.6L and 5.4L engines used a plastic intake manifold whose front coolant passage can crack with age and heat, letting coolant pour out with little warning.
issues.next: Pull over if the engine overheats. Replacement manifolds with a reinforced coolant crossover fix the problem for good.

issues.t: Head gasket failure (6.0L diesel)
issues.sym: Coolant disappearing with no visible leak, a coolant reservoir that bubbles or is pressurized, white exhaust smoke, or overheating when working hard.
issues.why: The 6.0L diesel holds its heads on with stretch-type bolts. Extra cylinder pressure, often after an oil cooler or EGR cooler failure or engine tuning, can stretch them and blow the head gaskets. Some E-Series owners report cracked heads and blocks.
issues.next: Stop driving if it is overheating or pushing coolant out. The lasting repair is new head gaskets with stronger head studs, and the coolers should be checked at the same time.

issues.t: Oil cooler clogs and EGR cooler cracks (6.0L diesel)
issues.sym: White steam-like smoke at startup, coolant loss, and overheating when loaded or towing.
issues.why: The engine oil cooler can clog with debris, which starves the EGR cooler of coolant. The overheated EGR cooler then cracks and lets coolant into the exhaust or intake.
issues.next: Have a diesel shop compare oil and coolant temperatures to check the oil cooler. Fixing it early can save the head gaskets.

issues.t: Injector control module (FICM) failure (6.0L diesel)
issues.sym: Hard or no starts when cold, rough idle, misfires or stalling, often worse with a weak battery.
issues.why: The module that fires the injectors sits on top of the engine. Heat, vibration and low battery voltage wear out its internal power supply.
issues.next: Have the module voltage tested and make sure the batteries are healthy. A rebuilt or upgraded module is the usual fix.

issues.t: Sticking turbo vanes and injectors (6.0L diesel)
issues.sym: Slow to build boost, poor power, rough running on cold starts that smooths out when warm, or oil leaking near the turbo drain tube.
issues.why: Soot can stick the turbo's adjustable vanes, and the oil-driven injectors are sensitive to oil quality and can stick, especially with overdue oil changes.
issues.next: Keep up with oil changes using diesel-rated oil. A shop can clean the turbo vanes; injector additives or injector replacement may be needed.

issues.t: 6.0L diesel may stall without warning (recall)
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: A wiring problem at the injector control module harness or oil pressure sensor connector could shut the engine off. Ford recalled these vans to upgrade the harness or connector.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the fix is free at a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor failure (7.3L diesel)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or will not start, and the tachometer may drop to zero while driving.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensor on the 7.3L Power Stroke fails intermittently. Ford recalled some trucks for it.
issues.next: Carry a spare if you rely on the van; the sensor is quick to replace. Check the connector too.

issues.t: Misfires from injector wiring or driver module (7.3L diesel)
issues.sym: Misfiring, rough running, lost power or stalling, often blamed on bad injectors at first.
issues.why: Connectors on the wiring harness under the valve covers fail, and the injector driver module in the fender area can be damaged by moisture.
issues.next: Have injector circuit codes read and the harness and module connectors checked before replacing injectors.

issues.t: Coolant contamination from injector sleeves or oil cooler (7.3L diesel)
issues.sym: Coolant loss, bubbles in the coolant, fuel smell in the coolant, or oil and coolant mixing.
issues.why: On high-mileage engines the injector sleeves can crack and let fuel into the coolant, and aged oil cooler seals can leak.
issues.next: Have the coolant tested for fuel or oil. Catching it early prevents bigger engine damage.

issues.t: Cruise control switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In rare cases there is smoke or a burning smell from the engine compartment, even with the van parked and off.
issues.why: A cruise control deactivation switch on the brake master cylinder can leak brake fluid internally, overheat and start an underhood fire. Ford recalled many trucks, vans and motorhome chassis to add a fused harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the cruise control switch recall and have the fused harness installed. Park outside until it is done.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping, delayed or harsh shifts, flaring between gears, or losing drive altogether, especially in heavily loaded vans.
issues.why: Heavy loads and heat wear out the automatic transmission. Owners of these years report full replacements around 90,000 to 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Change the fluid regularly, and consider an auxiliary cooler if you tow or carry heavy loads.

issues.t: Check engine light with transmission solenoid codes
issues.sym: Check engine light with transmission codes, sometimes with harsh or odd shifts.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for TorqShift automatics on these vans setting codes P0751, P0730 or P2700, on transmissions built before mid-December 2015.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about bulletin 16-0057 before replacing parts.

issues.t: Fuel tank lining breaks down and clogs the fuel system
issues.sym: Loss of power, stalling, hard starting or clogged fuel filters again and again.
issues.why: Owners report the coating inside the fuel tank coming apart and sending debris to the filters and pump.
issues.next: Have the fuel filter cut open and inspected. If you find tank debris, the tank usually has to be replaced and the fuel system cleaned.

issues.t: Fuel rail crossover hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell from the engine area or fuel dripping near the engine.
issues.why: The crossover hose on the 5.4L engine's fuel rail can crack and leak fuel, which is a fire risk. Ford recalled the vans to replace the fuel rail.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers quit, often in bad weather when you need them most.
issues.why: Some wiper motors left the factory without grease on the output gear, which can wear and break. Ford recalled these vans to inspect and grease the gear.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the wiper motor recall.

issues.t: Rear axle failure
issues.sym: Whining, clunking or grinding from the rear axle, then loss of drive.
issues.why: Owners report rear axle and drivetrain failures on heavily used vans around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the rear axle fluid checked for metal and the bearings inspected at the first sign of noise.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine dies in traffic, sometimes at low mileage, with power steering and brake assist dropping away.
issues.why: Owners of 2007 cutaways and 2013 vans report sudden shutdowns. Causes vary, so proper diagnosis is needed.
issues.next: Treat it as a safety problem. Have stored codes read right after it happens, and check for open recalls.

issues.t: Driver seat track can break in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning to the driver.
issues.why: A gear in the power driver seat track could fracture in a crash and let the seat move. Ford recalled these vans to inspect and replace it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the seat recall.

issues.t: Windshield may form bubbles in heat (recall)
issues.sym: Bubbles or distortion in the windshield, especially in hot weather, that make it hard to see.
issues.why: Some windshields were made under the wrong conditions. Ford recalled affected vans to replace them as needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the windshield recall.

issues.t: Seat bolts may break (recall)
issues.sym: No warning to the driver.
issues.why: Some bolts used to install seats were made incorrectly and could fracture. Ford recalled affected vehicles to replace them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: A/C cools poorly
issues.sym: Weak cooling, temperature that does not match the setting, or a check engine light with code P06A0.
issues.why: Ford issued a service message for poor A/C performance on vans and cutaways with the electronically controlled compressor.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about service message 47850 and have the A/C system and compressor controls tested.

issues.t: Trailer brake controller may not apply trailer brakes (recall)
issues.sym: When towing, the trailer brakes do not work or work weakly, so the van and trailer take longer to stop.
issues.why: Some vans with the factory trailer brake controller and the 6.8L engine had a software problem. Ford recalled them to reprogram the engine computer.
issues.next: Do not tow until the recall software is installed.

issues.t: Backup camera image may fail (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera picture is blank or wrong when backing up.
issues.why: Ford recalled some 2017-2019 vehicles for a rearview camera problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open camera recalls and use mirrors and a spotter until it is fixed.

issues.t: Engine cover can get too hot (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cover between the front seats gets very hot, with a hot smell in the cab. Passengers touching it can be burned.
issues.why: Insulation on the engine cover could be out of place and the engine's heat-management software let the cover overheat. Ford recalled these vehicles, then re-recalled some after incomplete software updates.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both engine cover recalls and keep people from resting against the cover until it is fixed.

issues.t: Power steering line can leak and cut brake assist (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden fluid leak, heavy steering and a hard brake pedal.
issues.why: On dual-rear-wheel models the power steering pressure line was not connected well at the hydraulic brake booster, so fluid could escape and take away both steering and brake assist.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls on this line. If steering suddenly gets heavy, slow down and stop safely.

issues.t: Wiring can rub through and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Stalling, or ABS and stability control warnings.
issues.why: A rear wiring harness could rub on the frame and damage fuel pump circuits. Ford recalled affected chassis.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Rear axle may be low on fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Whining or grinding from the rear axle, then possible axle failure.
issues.why: Some rear axles were filled below the minimum level at the factory. Ford recalled them to check and fill.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Fuel tank seam can rust and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or drips near the fuel tank.
issues.why: Paint on the fuel tank's weld seam can peel and let it corrode, which can lead to a leak and fire risk. Ford recalled these chassis to inspect and replace tanks as needed.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Rear brake rotor bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or vibration from a rear wheel; in the worst case a wheel could come off.
issues.why: Rear axle rotor bolts on some E-450 chassis may not have been tightened correctly. Ford recalled them to check the bolts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and stop driving if you hear new clunks from the rear wheels.

issues.t: Park may not hold the vehicle (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle can roll after being shifted into Park.
issues.why: A casting defect in the transmission can stop the park pawl from fully engaging. Ford recalled these vehicles to inspect and replace transmission parts.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Blower motor may fail and disable the defroster (recall)
issues.sym: The heater and defroster fan stops working and the windshield fogs or ices up.
issues.why: Some blower motors on vehicles built in spring 2025 can fail. Ford recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and do not drive if you cannot clear the windshield.

issues.t: Backup alarm may not sound (recall)
issues.sym: No beeping alarm when reversing.
issues.why: The backup alarm connector can loosen and come off. Ford recalled affected chassis.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and use a spotter when backing up.
